newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel drops sharply against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel drops sharply against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar on Thursday in very active trading, dealers said.
"We haven't seen such a heavy trading in a long time. Volume was high and the dollar rose sharply following its rise abroad," said Ilan Zadka at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The rise of the U.S. currency forced the Bank of Israel to intervene in the market to prevent the basket from falling on the scale of more than $200 million," Zadka said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for more than a month.

"Activity was boosted by the business sector, which converted foreign currency into shekels for end-of-the-month payments. Volume was also high because the banks will remain closed tomorrow," Zadka added.
Israeli bank employees are due to strike tomorrow for the third Friday in a row demanding a five-day work week.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3480 shekels against 3.3380 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6424 shekels against 3.6418 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7661 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7590 on Wednesday and against the mark at 1.9818 shekels against 1.9947 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3470 shekels.
